claim: Tissue cells tessellate approximately as hexagons / as a froth, the configuration that partitions area with least perimeter.

claim_decomposition.C1_mean_six_froth: Cells of a tissue are 'on the average hexagonal, but some will have fewer and some more sides than six' (p. 325) — the froth analogy (p. 305) implies a trivalent network with mean polygon side number 6 (Euler).
claim_decomposition.C2_hexagonal_optimum: 'the closely packed hexagons gave the minimal extent of boundary in a plane' (p. 330) and partitions meeting in threes at 120 degrees minimise partition area (Lamarle, p. 309) — the honeycomb is the least-perimeter equal-area partition (Hales 2001).
claim_decomposition.C3_near_regular_hexagons: 'The hexagonal pattern is illustrated among organisms in countless cases, but those in which the pattern is perfectly regular ... are not so numerous' (p. 321); 'wherever we have a system of cylinders or spheres ... in complete surface contact, there ... we tend to get a pattern of hexagons' (p. 323).

dataset_audit_entry.reason: Thompson's own 1917 figures / public-domain plates are fetchable from the pinned IA scan; loop digitises them.

rationale: Thompson's claim is about tissue cells in general (plant parenchyma, Elodea epidermis, 'hexagonal epithelium-cells of the pigment layer of the eye' p. 321, columnar intestinal epithelium p. 321, corals p. 325); it names no single species, so a monolayer epithelium of the eye is a direct instance, not an analogue.

Primary specimen: human corneal endothelium in situ (alizarin red outlines, Zhiguo He, CC BY-SA 4.0) — a single-layer ocular epithelium of ~150 fully visible polygonal cells; this is the modern standard tissue for polygon-class ('pleomorphism') analysis.

Secondary specimen: Elodea canadensis leaf epidermis micrograph (Daemon Canchig, CC BY-SA 4.0) — the SAME species Thompson drew in Fig. 126; elongated brick-like cells test his p. 322-323 remark that 'apparently quadrangular' elongated cells still meet three at a point.

Thompson's own 1917 figures in the 120-127 range are line drawings, not photographs: Fig. 124 is an idealised schematic and Fig. 126 has only 8 cells, so they cannot by themselves yield a polygon-class distribution. Fig. 125 (Rhumbler soap froth, ~100 cells) is digitised as the physical froth reference the claim invokes.
